body:
Chief: FIRST SWEEP SLICE PRE-SCOPED so nobody waits on me when the reference lands. bd-01M16BFTZNPEP1VAXDGWDBTE4G, P1, unassigned, BLOCKED until the population reference shape is on main - copy that shape, do not invent one.

Ten embed-core types, exact files and lines on the bead, ordered by what each certifies rather than by file: ValidatedVector first, because its of() rejects dimension mismatch, non-finite values, non-normalized vectors and the zero vector, and a forged one makes every downstream distance and neighbour ranking compute on NaN while announcing itself as validated. Then the privacy carriers, then identity, then the rest.

I COMPUTED THE REFERENCE SCOPE RATHER THAN GUESSING IT, per the rule that cost us a failed gate an hour ago: embed-core, embed-bench AND embed-grakern all reference these types, so all three are in the gate. embed-grakern is JVM-only; embed-core is cross-built. The exact gate line is on the bead, unpiped.

AND I WROTE DOWN WHAT NOT TO DO, because the last candidate over-closed before I caught it: one door only, fromProduct. No probes for copy, which a private constructor already suppresses - I verified that with a control rather than by absence. No probes for unapply, _1, _2 or Product, which construct nothing and expose only what the public accessors already do. None of these ten hides a field, so the rule-8 exception does not apply to any of them.

The evidence standard is m1's and it is binding: demonstrate the forge in one line, do not assert it. Start with ValidatedVector - and if fromProduct does NOT produce a NaN or unnormalized vector there, say so loudly, because then my 45-count is wrong and I will withdraw it rather than defend it.
